title: [route_check] route_check is still reporting transient route mismatch
author: bingwang-ms
body:

**Description**

<!--
Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->
The route_check is configured to check routes every 5 minutes, and report an error after 3 consecutive failures. In other words, it shouldn't detect and report transient route mismatch as an error. 
```
check program routeCheck with path "/usr/bin/route_check.py"
    every 5 cycles
    if status != 0 for 3 cycle then alert repeat every 1 cycles
```
But following error message was even observed when running test_lag[single_lag]

```
Nov  2 15:14:15.386212 str-7260cx3-acs-2 ERR route_check.py:  results: { {#012    "Unaccounted_ROUTE_ENTRY_TABLE_entries": [#012        "10.0.0.34/31", #012        "2064:100::26/128", #012        "fc00::24/126"#012    ]#012} }'
Nov  2 15:14:15.386731 str-7260cx3-acs-2 ERR route_check.py:  Failed. Look at reported mismatches above
```

I added some log in check_route to record result of each cycle, and found that monit didn't respect the configuration.
```
Nov  4 06:22:47.927266 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 06:27:51.662057 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!

Nov  4 06:48:03.029133 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 06:53:05.833791 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 06:58:09.176143 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:03:12.164442 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:08:14.528038 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:13:17.977604 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:18:21.176402 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:23:23.286864 str-7260cx3-acs-2 INFO route_check.py: All good!
Nov  4 07:28:27.017173 str-7260cx3-acs-2 ERR route_check.py:  results: { {#012    "missed_ROUTE_TABLE_routes": [#012        "10.0.0.34/31", #012        "100.1.0.35/32", #012        "fc00::24/126"#012    ]#012} }
```
We can see that route_check reported the error even all checks before are successful.

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Run ```pc/test_lag_2.py```. The issue was not easy to repro. I runned test_lag_2 for many times but repro only once.
2. 

**Describe the results you received:**
check_route reported transient route mismatch in test_lag_2[single_lag]

**Describe the results you expected:**
check_route shouldn't reported transient route mismatch as error.

**Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):**
This issue is observed on SONiC.20191130.52 and SONiC.master.466-f2a258ac

linkedPullRequests.title: [route_check]Add an option for route_check to control whether log is writen to syslog
linkedPullRequests.author: bingwang-ms
linkedPullRequests.body:
<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:

If you are adding/modifying/removing any command or utility script, please also
make sure to add/modify/remove any unit tests from the tests
directory as appropriate.

If you are modifying or removing an existing 'show', 'config' or 'sonic-clear'
subcommand, or you are adding a new subcommand, please make sure you also
update the Command Line Reference Guide (doc/Command-Reference.md) to reflect
your changes.

Please provide the following information:
-->
Fix https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/5804
**- What I did**
By default, route_check.py will report an ERROR in syslog if route mismatch is detected, which is out of the control of monit config file and cause LogAnalyzer to report test error. This commit add an option (-s) to control this behavior. And log is not writen to syslog in default.

**- How I did it**
Add an option (-s) for ```route_checker.py```.

**- How to verify it**
The update is verified on Arista-7260.
1. Add a static route whose nexthop is not reachable.
```
ip route add 1.1.1.1 via 192.168.1.101
```
2. Run ```route_check.py```, and error msg is only printed on stdout. Nothing is writen to syslog
3. Run ```route_check.py -s```. and error msg is writen to both stdout and syslog
4. Wait for 15 minutes, and confirm that monit will report the error
```
Nov  4 09:30:36.917367 str-7260cx3-acs-2 ERR monit[631]: 'routeCheck' status failed (255) -- results: { {#012    "missed_ROUTE_TABLE_routes": [#012        "1.1.1.1/32"#012    ]#012} }#012 Failed. Look at reported mismatches above
```


**- Previous command output (if the output of a command-line utility has changed)**
Output is not changed.

**- New command output (if the output of a command-line utility has changed)**
Output is not changed.
